original_test_intent: Verify that an approved PCIe link detects and reports a correctable Bad DLLP event, performs the expected link-layer recovery and keeps the attached device/service available without escalation.
original_method: Do not execute from the current label. Future method must map both sides of one link, baseline link/AER/replay counters, inject one vendor-defined Bad DLLP in an approved direction, correlate the Bad DLLP-specific status and replay response, then prove link width/speed, driver, device I/O and counters return to the acceptance state.
manual_activity: The PCIe/NVIDIA owner defines the exact Bad DLLP corruption mechanism and link direction, selects one safe endpoint/root-port pair, supervises injection and restores link/device state.
required_inputs: Pinned NVIDIA PCIe RAS injector/spec/version/checksum and supported firmware/OS
Endpoint/root-port/slot/BDF/link topology with injection side and traffic direction
Exact Bad DLLP stimulus semantics, affected DLLP field and proof of correctable classification
Expected Bad DLLP-specific endpoint/root-port AER status, root reporting, replay/counter delta and timeout
No link loss/retrain escalation, no fatal/non-fatal AER, device I/O continuity and performance tolerance
Clear policy, independent OOB recovery, aborts and restoration
safety_requirements: Keep execution blocked until the Bad DLLP procedure and Criteria are approved
Use an isolated test link/SUT with independent console/OOB and recoverable device workload
Record AER masks/status, link/replay counters and device traffic baseline without destructive clears
Inject once on one mapped direction; abort on replay storm, unexpected retrain, link down, severe AER, device loss or I/O corruption
Capture evidence before owner-approved clear and restore all injection/mask/link state
agent_execution_scope: Collect read-only topology, link state, AER and replay counters, logs and device workload health
Check future Bad DLLP procedure against the mapped link and evidence oracle
Do not select/corrupt DLLPs, configure injector or AER masks, clear status, retrain/reset, recover, retry or judge result
engineer_actions: Publish the Bad DLLP-specific command and Criteria
Approve injection direction, exact link, status and replay oracle
Verify device integrity and issue verdict

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Apply one defined Bad DLLP to one mapped link and demonstrate target-specific correctable status and bounded replay while link and I/O stay healthy.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Transforms the label into required direction, packet-layer, AER, replay and continuity checkpoints without selecting an unapproved command.

project_override_considerations: Injection capability and observability can reside at the endpoint, root port or lab interposer; the project must identify the authoritative locus. Bad TLP evidence is not accepted for this variant.
expected_evidence: Approved Bad DLLP injector/spec and endpoint-root-port-BDF-direction map
Baseline AER masks/status, link width/speed/state, replay counters and device I/O
Exact one-shot malformed-DLLP transcript and synchronized timeline
Fresh Bad DLLP-specific status/root report and bounded replay/counter delta at the mapped link
No link loss, severe AER, device reset/disconnect, I/O error or unacceptable performance impact
Cleared/restored state diff and engineer verdict

review_improvement: Separates this duplicate-titled row by its link-layer DLLP coverage and adds replay plus device-continuity evidence specific to that fault.
independent_technical_reasoning: DLLPs govern link-layer flow control and reliability, whereas TLPs carry transactions. A generic correctable error or Bad TLP record would not establish Bad DLLP handling. The test must bind a single malformed DLLP to a known link direction and show bounded replay without retrain or I/O disruption; those essentials are absent from the source.
